feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: For some patients, psychedelic treatment brings new troubles in its aftermath
entry.summary: Psychedelics could transform mental health care, but some advocates and researchers say there needs to be more focus on the minority of people with persistent troubles after using these drugs.

entry.title: Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya Muslim minority, court rules
entry.summary: The International Court of Justice has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya Muslim minority — a landmark judgment that marks a turning point in international justice.

entry.title: A new concerto highlights an instrument usually in the background: the timpani
entry.summary: The Seattle Symphony is premiering a new concerto that spotlights a solo performance of an instrument pretty rarely featured in such solos: the timpani.

entry.title: The AI boom is the biggest gold rush San Francisco's seen yet
entry.summary: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer talks with Ben Steverman of Bloomberg about how the incredible amount of wealth generated by AI startups is transforming the San Francisco Bay Area.

entry.title: How non-player characters in 'Grand Theft Auto VI' help create its big world
entry.summary: In video games, "barks" are short lines of dialogue given to various characters in the world. Grand Theft Auto VI proves how this kind of dialogue contributes to an immersive world.

entry.title: On her latest album, Snoh Aalegra remembers a 'Legendary Love'
entry.summary: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer talks with singer Snoh Aalegra about her new album Legendary Love, the relationship that inspired it and her many influences.

entry.title: The cost of college is confusing. Some schools are trying to change that
entry.summary: A growing number of colleges are trying to reduce widespread public confusion about what college actually costs.

entry.title: In Elsinore, Andrew Scott plays actor dying from AIDS as he plays Hamlet
entry.summary: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Andrew Scott about starring as the late actor Ian Charleson in the movie Elsinore and about what his final performance as Hamlet meant.

entry.title: Why the U.S. air traffic control system still relies on an 'antique' network
entry.summary: The FAA says the telecom outage that led to Friday's nationwide ground stop began with an upgrade to fiber-optic cables. Industry experts say the work is long overdue.

entry.title: For new members of Congress, getting a prime office is a game of chance
entry.summary: Orientation for incoming House members is coming to a close. After two weeks of training, leadership elections and happy hours, one of the last rites of passage is the office lottery.
